h1: The 6 Best Storage Carts for Makeup of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Makeup Storage Carts: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six rolling makeup carts scored on drawer layout, display space, wheel locks, footprint and how well each sorts a collection.
summary: The Hongtamoya four-drawer cart is our top pick, with classified storage and the flexibility to roll or sit fixed. The SUNALLY adds lockable wheels at a lower price, the open-shelf and display-case cart suits collectors, and the ZQUYAJ and SWTYMIKI are slim options. The Goovilla is the cheapest way to start.
intro: A makeup cart usually fails for a reason that has nothing to do with makeup. It is the wheels. A cart that rolls freely is wonderful for moving from vanity to bathroom, and a menace when you press a drawer shut and the whole thing drifts. Lockable wheels, or the option to use the cart fixed in place, decide whether it stays useful.

We ranked six rolling carts by what their listings state: drawer count and type, display or open-shelf space, wheel design and footprint. Most pages say little about weight limits or exact sizes, so we flag that and score the layout claims. The right cart is the one that matches how you sort, not the one with the most tiers.

products.name: Hongtamoya Makeup Cart Organizer with 4 Drawers
products.verdict: Four drawers for classified storage, usable rolling or fixed.
products.description:
Hongtamoya offers a makeup cart with four drawers, large capacity, classified storage and a mobile-and-fixed use design.

It wins because four drawers let you sort by category, skincare in one, brushes in another, palettes in a third, which beats a single big tray where everything migrates to the bottom. The mobile-and-fixed design means you can lock it in place when you work and roll it when you clean, a benefit the open-wheel designs lack.

Buy it for a growing collection that needs real categories. The listing gives no dimensions or weight limit, so measure your space before ordering and avoid loading the top with heavy items.
products.idealFor: Growing collections that need real categories.
products.skipIf: You want a slim cart that fits under a desk.

products.name: SUNALLY Makeup Cart Organizer with Drawer, 3 Tier Rolling Makeup Cart
products.verdict: Three tiers, a removable drawer and lockable wheels, all under $25.
products.description:
SUNALLY is a three-tier rolling cart with a removable drawer and lockable wheels. The listing highlights large capacity and classified storage.

It ranks second because lockable wheels fix the drawer-drift problem, and the removable drawer lets you carry a day's makeup to the mirror. It costs well under the Hongtamoya, though it gives you fewer enclosed compartments, so loose items on open tiers show dust.

Buy it for a shared bathroom or small vanity where you want to roll away the cart at night and keep the counter clear for the morning rush. The listing offers no weight limit, so keep the heaviest bottles on the lowest tier and lock the wheels before loading.
products.idealFor: Small vanities and shared bathrooms on a budget.
products.skipIf: You want fully enclosed drawers for everything.

products.name: Makeup Organizer Cart with Drawers Make Up Organizers for Vanity
products.verdict: A floor cart with a divided cosmetic display case up top and an open shelf in the middle.
products.description:
This floor-standing makeup organizer combines a top divisional cosmetic display case, a middle open shelf and drawers, billed as the newest floor makeup organizer.

It ranks third because the display case suits collectors who want lipsticks and palettes visible, and the open shelf takes taller items such as skincare bottles. It is a stationary-feeling design next to the Hongtamoya, and the listing does not describe wheels.

Buy it for a vanity corner where display matters as much as storage, and where a collection of palettes, lip products and brushes deserves to be seen. Without wheel information, plan for it to stay in place, and confirm the drawer count on the live page before you order.
products.idealFor: Collectors who want makeup visible and sorted.
products.skipIf: You need a cart you can roll between rooms.

products.name: ZQUYAJ Rolling Makeup Organizer Cart with 3 Drawers Under Desk Storage
products.verdict: Three removable fabric drawers and display cases, sized to roll under a desk.
products.description:
ZQUYAJ lists a rolling cart with three removable fabric drawers, top divisional cosmetic display cases and a space-saving rolling design for under-desk storage.

It ranks fourth because fabric drawers are lighter and quieter than plastic but hold less shape under heavy bottles. The top display cases and under-desk fit are its points, and it beats the Goovilla on layout though not on price.

Buy it for a desk-based vanity or dorm room where floor space is scarce. Fabric drawers sag with heavy palettes, so keep weighty items in the base, spread the load across all three drawers, and use small dividers inside each one to stop products sliding when you roll the cart.
products.idealFor: Desk vanities and dorm rooms with little floor space.
products.skipIf: You store heavy bottles and glass jars.

products.name: SWTYMIKI Rolling Makeup Organizer Cart
products.verdict: Three spacious drawers and an elegant Nordic look that moves out of the bathroom.
products.description:
SWTYMIKI is a rolling cart with three spacious drawers for easy categorization and an elegant Nordic aesthetic. The listing notes you can move it out from the bathroom.

It ranks fifth because its pitch is style and movement, with fewer practical details than the SUNALLY on wheel locks or removable drawers. Three drawers match the ZQUYAJ in number, but there is no display case on top.

Buy it for a bedroom or bathroom where the cart is on view and should look intentional. Check the wheel and drawer materials on the live page, as the listing does not state them, and look for lockable casters before you commit to rolling it across a hard floor.
products.idealFor: Style-conscious users who keep the cart on view.
products.skipIf: You want a display top or documented wheel locks.

products.name: Goovilla Rolling Makeup Organizer Cart with Removable Drawer
products.verdict: A practical starter with a detachable drawer and four 360-degree swivel wheels.
products.description:
Goovilla sells a practical makeup cart with a detachable drawer and four 360-degree swivel wheels. It sits under $25.

It ranks last because it has only one drawer, so categories overlap, and the listing states no wheel locks. Its strength is the price and the detachable drawer, which carries a day's products to the mirror.

Buy it as a first cart for a small collection of daily essentials, or as a spare caddy for hair tools and nail supplies. As the collection grows, plan to move up to the Hongtamoya, since a single drawer sorts very little and the open tiers collect dust.
products.idealFor: First-time cart buyers with a small collection.
products.skipIf: You need several categories of storage.

methodology.title: Drawer layout
methodology.description: Count and type of drawers decide how well a cart sorts, so four-drawer and multi-tier layouts scored above single-drawer designs.

methodology.title: Display and open space
methodology.description: Divisional display cases and open shelves show off collections and take tall bottles, which we credited.

methodology.title: Wheels and mobility
methodology.description: Lockable wheels, swivel casters and fixed-use options decide whether the cart stays put when you press a drawer.

methodology.title: Footprint
methodology.description: Under-desk designs and slim carts suit small rooms; we weighed that against storage volume.

methodology.title: Value
methodology.description: Prices run from under $25 to $100, and we compared stated features to cost, marking down carts with vague listings.

whatMatters.detail: Drawers let you sort by category, which keeps a collection usable as it grows. Fabric drawers are light but sag, plastic ones hold shape, and removable drawers carry products to the mirror. Count the drawers in the title, think about how many categories you actually keep, and avoid single-drawer carts if you own more than basics.

A rolling cart drifts when you press a drawer shut unless the wheels lock. The SUNALLY lists lockable wheels, the Goovilla lists four 360-degree swivel wheels. Check the wheel line in the bullets, and if locks are not mentioned, assume a freely rolling cart and plan to place it against a wall.

A display case or open shelf shows lipsticks, palettes and brushes at a glance, which saves digging. Several carts here add a divisional top. Pick one if you like seeing your collection, and skip it if dust and sunlight bother you, since open cases collect both. Sun and warmth shorten the life of lipsticks and foundations, so keep the cart away from windows.

Cart size decides where it can live. An under-desk model like the ZQUYAJ slides into a gap, while a floor cart with a display top needs a clear corner. Measure the width, depth and height of your space and compare it with the stated dimensions, which many listings omit. Leave a few inches around the cart so drawers can open fully and the wheels can turn.

Makeup is lighter than most storage, but glass bottles and large palettes add up. The listings give no weight limits. Keep heavy items on the bottom tier, check whether drawers are fabric or plastic, and be cautious about stacking a lot of skincare on the top shelf, which makes a tall cart top-heavy and prone to tipping on a thick rug.

howToChoose.intro: Drawers do the sorting, so pick the count that matches your categories.

faq.q: Can these carts fit under a desk?
faq.a: The ZQUYAJ is explicitly built for under-desk storage, with a space-saving rolling design. The others do not list that use. Measure your desk's clearance against the stated height before ordering, because a cart that is half an inch too tall will not slide in and cannot be trimmed.

faq.q: What is the usual mistake with makeup carts?
faq.a: Overlooking wheel locks. A cart that rolls when you push a drawer is frustrating. The SUNALLY lists lockable wheels, and the Hongtamoya works fixed, so prefer those if your floor is smooth, and test the lock before you load the drawers.

faq.q: Is the Hongtamoya worth it over the SUNALLY?
faq.a: For a large collection, yes. Four drawers sort more categories than three tiers. If you want lockable wheels and the lowest price, the SUNALLY wins, but it has fewer enclosed compartments, so more of your products sit exposed to dust.

faq.q: How should I set up a makeup cart?
faq.a: Put heavy items on the lowest tier, group by category in drawers, and keep daily items on top. On the Hongtamoya, assign one drawer per category. Lock the wheels before you start applying, and keep a small tray on top for the items you reach for every day.

faq.q: How do I clean a makeup cart?
faq.a: Wipe plastic and wood surfaces with a damp cloth, shake out fabric drawers on the ZQUYAJ and SWTYMIKI, and dust display cases often. Remove spills quickly, since foundation can stain fabric, and let drawers dry fully before refilling them.

faq.q: Are open display tops a good idea?
faq.a: They look good but gather dust and expose products to light and humidity. For items you use daily, an open case is fine. Store rarely used or sensitive products in a closed drawer, such as in the SUNALLY's removable one, away from light and steam.

finalTake: The Hongtamoya four-drawer cart is the one to buy: real categories, large capacity and a mobile-or-fixed design. The SUNALLY is the budget pick with lockable wheels, and the display-case cart suits collectors who want their makeup on show. The ZQUYAJ fits under a desk, the SWTYMIKI is the stylish option, and the Goovilla is a starter for a small collection.
